draft.title: Completing the square
card: A monic quadratic has x² with a coefficient of 1, such as x² + 6x + 2. Completed square form looks like (x + p)² + q.
Take half the coefficient of x, then square it. Add that square and take it away, so the value of the expression does not change.
The x² term, the x term and the added square make a perfect square: x² + 6x + 9 = (x + 3)². Whatever is left over goes outside the bracket.
Example: x² + 6x + 2. Half of 6 is 3, and 3² = 9. So x² + 6x + 9 − 9 + 2 = (x + 3)² − 7.
draft.remember: Halve the x coefficient, square it, add it and take it away.

a.q: Which is x² + 10x + 3 in completed square form?
a.why: Half of 10 is 5, and 5² = 25. So x² + 10x + 25 − 25 + 3 = (x + 5)² − 22. Taking away 25 but forgetting to add the 3 gives (x + 5)² − 25, which is wrong.
a.clue: Half of 10 goes inside the bracket. Then use its square.

b.q: Mia writes x² − 8x + 5 in completed square form. What does she get?
b.why: Half of −8 is −4, and (−4)² = 16. So x² − 8x + 16 − 16 + 5 = (x − 4)² − 11. Using +21 comes from adding 16 instead of taking it away. Check by expanding: (x − 4)² − 11 = x² − 8x + 16 − 11 = x² − 8x + 5.
b.clue: Half of a negative number is still negative, and the bracket keeps that sign.

check.summary: No problems found. Both questions have exactly one correct option, and the card, remember line, clues and explanations agree.

final.title: Completing the square
card: A monic quadratic has \(x^{2}\) with a coefficient of 1, such as \(x^{2} + 6x + 2\). Completed square form looks like \((x + p)^{2} + q\).
Take half the coefficient of \(x\), then square it. Add that square and take it away, so the value of the expression does not change.
The \(x^{2}\) term, the \(x\) term and the added square make a perfect square: \(x^{2} + 6x + 9 = (x + 3)^{2}\). Whatever is left over goes outside the bracket.
final.remember: Halve the \(x\) coefficient, square it, add it and take it away.

a.q: Which is \(x^{2} + 10x + 3\) in completed square form?
a.why: Half of 10 is 5, and \(5^{2} = 25\). So \(x^{2} + 10x + 25 - 25 + 3 = (x + 5)^{2} - 22\). Taking away 25 but forgetting to add the 3 gives \((x + 5)^{2} - 25\), which is wrong.
a.clue: Half of 10 goes inside the bracket. Then use its square.

b.q: Mia writes \(x^{2} - 8x + 5\) in completed square form. What does she get?
b.why: Half of \(-8\) is \(-4\), and \((-4)^{2} = 16\). So \(x^{2} - 8x + 16 - 16 + 5 = (x - 4)^{2} - 11\). Using \(+21\) comes from adding 16 instead of taking it away. Check by expanding: \((x - 4)^{2} - 11\) is \(x^{2} - 8x + 16 - 11\), which is \(x^{2} - 8x + 5\).
b.clue: Half of a negative number is still negative, and the bracket keeps that sign.
